info.title: sys-con
info.author: cathery, o0Zz
info.description: Use USB controllers from other consoles on Nintendo Switch.
info.details:
sys-con is a sysmodule that adds support for third-party USB controllers.

It supports a wide range of HID and XInput-compatible gamepads, including PlayStation, Xbox, PC controllers, arcade sticks, wheels, and other USB input devices. Controllers can be used in docked mode or through a compatible USB-C OTG adapter in handheld mode.

Configuration files under `sd:/config/sys-con/` allow you to customize button mappings, stick and trigger behavior, deadzones, polling settings, controller profiles, and other device-specific options.

changelog:
2.1.0

# Changelog
   - Added Xbox Wireless Adapter support (needs Microsoft's firmware, see the README). Thanks to @hagenbui
   - Added USB keyboard and mouse support
   - Added sideways single Joy-Con mode for games that only accept single Joy-Cons
   - Reworked MITM mode, now the default. Fixes the freeze in Super Mario 3D All-Stars (#128)
   - Fixed `discovery_mode`, stick direction bindings and the network pad's vertical axis                                                 
   - Fixed several controller detection, sleep and config parsing issues

  # Upgrading from 2.0.0
  If you keep your own config.ini, flip the sign of any `lstick_up/down` or `rstick_up/down` bound to an axis (`lstick_up=+Y` becomes     
  `lstick_up=-Y`).
